You are correct (and your cousin is wrong). There are some more cards like short
term investment where you are not allowed to play mastercards when you use them
but that is clearly stated on the cards.(the only one I can think of at the moment
is protracted investment). Remember however that if you play out of turn master
cards, like sudden reversal, this forfeits your next master phase action.

>
>
> 2nd question if i bleed and my prey announce that his vampire blocks which to
> block you have to tap right and then i play a modifer to increase my stealth
> and he cant increase his intercept doesnt his vampire stayed taped or does he
> just announce his vampire blocks but doesnt tap untill its succesful?

A minion taps when he blocks, but if he cant play enough intercept to match up to
your stelth his vampire is untapped again. The only way you can prevent this is to
play a card that states he cant untap (e.g. superior Faceless night).

> and Ghoul deck would be nice. No?

From the discussions on this NG it seems that VoTC are not planning any more
expansions, which is a pity.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Joshi24 wrote:
>
> My cousin insist that your only allowed one master card action total but i
> almost certain that the rules say you are only allowed to play one master card
> but ones that you already have out like hunting ground cards etc you can tap as
> many as you want. The only one i think were you tap and thats all you get is
> the short term investment one.

You get one Master Phase Action each master phase.
You can use this action only to play a master card.
Using a card in play (including a master card) doesn't require
spending a Master Phase Action.
Using a master card in play doesn't require tapping that master card.

(Add "unless otherwise noted on card text" to each sentence above).

> 2nd question if i bleed and my prey announce that his vampire blocks which to
> block you have to tap right and then i play a modifer to increase my stealth
> and he cant increase his intercept doesnt his vampire stayed taped or does he
> just announce his vampire blocks but doesnt tap untill its succesful?

The blocking minion isn't tapped until the block is successful.
[Rulebook: section 18.2]

> Also when is Wizard going to bring out more expansion decks a Vampire hunter
> and Ghoul deck would be nice. No?

No more expansions are currently planned.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In article <19980128045...@ladder03.news.aol.com>, Joshi24
<jos...@aol.com> writes

>My cousin insist that your only allowed one master card action total but i
>almost certain that the rules say you are only allowed to play one master card
>but ones that you already have out like hunting ground cards etc you can tap as
>many as you want. The only one i think were you tap and thats all you get is
>the short term investment one.
>

Actually, you don't tap it. You just take a pool off it.

The way your master phase goes is this, basically:

You have ONE master phase action by default unless you use a card like
The Parthenon, Anson or Rumors of Gehenna.

With your ONE master phase action you can take ONE master phase action.
Playing a master card is a master phase action. Also, using a Short
Term Investment is a master phase action.

However, using a Blood Doll ISN'T a master phase action because it
simply says "during your master phase". A card has to specifically
state that it costs a master phase action to work for it to replace your
one playable master card. Another example, other than the various
Investment style cards (Short Term, Protracted and others), is Strained
Vitae Supply which you can get rid of using your pool which you put on
it as a Master Phase Action.

You are also confused about how Hunting Ground cards work. You play
them during your master phase as a master phase action but they work
during your untap phase. This includes all of them, even a few which
are printed incorrectly (the Tremere (Circle with a Triangle symbol)
have an incorrect Academic Hunting Ground) and you don't have to tap
them. But you only have to tap a master card if it says to, and there
is no such text on a Hunting Ground card.

>2nd question if i bleed and my prey announce that his vampire blocks which to
>block you have to tap right and then i play a modifer to increase my stealth
>and he cant increase his intercept doesnt his vampire stayed taped or does he
>just announce his vampire blocks but doesnt tap untill its succesful?
>

He doesn't tap until it is successful. People often tap them as a
convention just to indicate who is blocking but technically they don't
tap, otherwise you'd never be able to play any intercept reaction cards
(because you would be tapped).

>Also when is Wizard going to bring out more expansion decks a Vampire hunter
>and Ghoul deck would be nice. No?

It's going to be difficult to convince them to release any more unless
their profits go up from V:TES (so keep buying the cards that are there
already and just tell yourself it's for the general good).

There already are enough cards to make a Vampire hunter type deck
because you have all of the allies. Muddled Vampire Hunter with a
Sengir Dagger, Renegade Garou with one (using it on his second strike),
Order of Hermes Cabal (1R agg damage anyway) and so on do pretty well.
But the thing that most people want to see added are the "missing"
Sabbat clans - the Ravnos antitribu, Assamite antitribu and Serpents of
the Light, together with more Giovanni (not antitribu) and all of the
clans from the expansions (Lasombra, Tzimisce, Ravnos, Assamites,
Giovanni, Followers of Set) to make them playable. In fact, there's a
mailing list for exactly that purpose, dedicated to making cards for use
on Jyhad On-Line.

Go to http://www.ugcs.caltech.edu/~justinf/jyhad/

Various things there. Justin Fang's e-mail address (I won't put it here
so he doesn't get buckets of spam), links to the states of playtest
games, card lists for the new cards (with texts etc), discipline match
list (for all, including new, vamps) and so on.

People argue over the cards and suggest new ones on a mailing list run
by Justin Fang (so e-mail him if you want to join).

The aim is to get them into a state where they can be put forward as
JOL's own cards which anyone can use and (the following is a pipe dream)
get some form of official recognition from Wizards if they can't be
bothered to print a new expansion.

If you want details on Jyhad On-Line, go to http://deckserver.net

Follow the link to Jyhad On-Line and then you can see house rules,
deckserver commands and the like. All the cards in your deck are held
at the "deckserver" which you access with e-mail commands and basically
you play a game of Jyhad by e-mail (and they can be surprisingly quick -
one of them ones I'm on at the moment is just on its ninth time round
the table and two players just fell, one after the other (to a bleed and
having to *put* a pool on Smiling Jack, not burn pool for him)).

You can see the game states and histories by clicking on the links to
JOLXX, PlaytestX, JOLTXX (the tournament) or whatever.

If you can get access to e-mail a couple of times a day (or just think,
well, this isn't going to bother me at the moment so I'll only go on
once a day at the moment and wait for stuff to affect me (eg my
predator's turn) before I carry on). Normal Jyhad On-Line, using the
actual printed cards, has 8 players on a table (so Conservative
Agitation can be very useful ;). The Playtest games (run (moderated) by
people who are on the playtest list) normally have 6 players but there
is an 8 player game about to start (Chris Berger) and a four player one
will be got ready in a couple of weeks (run by, er, me).
